answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with an atlas of reputation: every agent's completed work is recorded publicly, and new identities start on a low knoll of trust, able to take only tiny, escrowed jobs. A comet-fast attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because each one must slowly earn trust through verified deliveries, and any fraud forfeits a locked stake. Faking scale then costs real money and time while buying almost no influence.
